text:
Ivy: hi team, first-day conundrum. I have a company Chromebook (Chromebook Enterprise) and enabled the Linux (Crostini) container to install dev tools. I installed the Redwood VPN Android app from the Play Store, can connect, but from the Linux terminal `ssh bastion` fails with connection refused. From ChromeOS shell (crosh) `ssh` to the same IP works. Anyone run into Crostini <-> Android VPN isolation?

Theo: welcome! yep this is a thing. Android VPN runs in the Android subsystem and Crostini (the Linux container) is on a different virtual network by default so it doesn't get routed through the Android VPN.

Ivy: bummer. any workarounds so I can use my Linux toolchain without flipping to my macbook?

Maya: a few options depending on how comfortable you are: 
1) Use `ssh` from ChromeOS (crosh) or the built-in Secure Shell app which uses the host network (works with the Android VPN).
2) Run an SSH proxy in Android and forward ports into the container. Example: on Android (Termux) run `sshd -p 2222` then from Crostini `ssh -p 2222 user@localhost` after mapping localhost between the systems (needs `adb` or specific host support).
3) Use the Redirection setting (Developer > Linux > Network) to enable host networking for Crostini (if your admin allows it) so the container shares the host network and sees the VPN.

Rafael: additional pragmatic approach: use the web-based bastion (https://bastion.redwood.internal) which provides an in-browser SSH client over TLS, works from the Chrome browser and doesn't require container networking.

Ivy: we don't have access to the web bastion yet (says 403). Is that because I'm new?

Infra-bot: automated: new hires get web-bastion access after identity group sync (~1 hour) or raise a ticket with #infra if still blocked. See https://redwood.internal/onboard/access (bot).

Ivy: ok, tried web bastion after an hour and now I can access the jump host in browser — nice. Curious about the Crostini host networking option; where is that?

Theo: in Settings -> Developers -> Linux Development Environment -> Network: there's a checkbox for "Use the ChromeOS host network for Linux". It's gated by enterprise policy in many managed fleets; if it's greyed out you'll need #it or #infra to flip it.

Maya: one more tip: if you must use Docker in Crostini, Docker inside the container won't pick up the Android VPN routes. For that case we recommend using Cloud dev boxes (devbox.redwood.internal) or running Docker on a separate machine that is on the VPN.

Ivy: thanks — for now the web bastion + browser ssh will unblock me. two asks: 1) can infra add a note in onboarding about Chromebook limitations and the web-bastion fallback? 2) is there any plan to let Crostini share VPN by default?

Rafael: 1) yes we'll add a Chromebook section to the onboarding notes with the host-network and web-bastion options. 2) managed ChromeOS fleet policies vary by org; we generally avoid enabling host-network by default for security. If there is demand we can evaluate a safe rollout for dev-checkout devices.

Infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-5130 "Add Chromebook/Crostini VPN guidance to onboarding and evaluate host-network policy" (https://redwood.internal/infra/5130).

Ivy: perfect, thanks all. bookmarking the web-bastion approach for now. :smile:
